article.articleHeadline: Spread of bacteria reinforces the importance of prevention in tilapia farming.
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus agalactiae serotype III is expanding in Brazilian tilapia farming, shifting from Northeast outbreaks to broader production hubs and intensifying sanitary challenges. The 26-week rollout covers more than 5,300 release points across the city center and districts such as Uvaranas, Oficinas, Cará-Cará, Contorno, Colônia Dona Luiza, Chapada and Ronda. The Wolbachia bacteria is transmitted to offspring, with the aim of reducing transmission of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Paraná’s technology began in July 2024 in Londrina and Foz do Iguaçu; Curitiba started on July 29, 2026 (Sítio Cercado), and Cascavel began Oct 19 across 17 neighborhoods. Ponta Grossa’s release follows a biofactory setup to prepare mosquitoes; ovitrampas monitor Wolbachia establishment. Partnerships include the Municipal Health Department, the Ministry of Health, Fiocruz, and Wolbito do Brasil. In Niterói, Rio de Janeiro, dengue cases dropped 89% where the approach covers the city.

Transmission occurs through contact with infected animals, particularly via scratches and bites, or when the fungus enters the skin through wounds. Suspected lesions in animals or humans should prompt veterinary or medical evaluation. Public health messaging emphasizes awareness and appropriate care to reduce transmission risk. Early diagnosis and treatment for both animal and human cases help protect the health of the population in Itajaí and the broader Santa Catarina region. The report underscores prevention, monitoring, and timely veterinary and health services as key strategies.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Bunia: 20,000 people per day subjected to health screening in Mudzibala - ACP
article.articleSummary: At the Mudzibala border health checkpoint near Bunia, Ituri, in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, about 20,000 people are screened daily as part of Ebola virus disease prevention. The screening includes handwashing, temperature checks, and visual observation to identify signs of illness. Travelers originate from Iga-Barrière and Mongbwalu in Djugu territory, and from Mahagi and Aru territories. A system is in place to retrieve passersby who attempt to evade the screening to ensure compliance with preventive measures. At the start of the outbreak, mistrust existed with many denying Ebola’s existence; a multidisciplinary team has since secured the submission of passersby at this checkpoint. Surveillance at this strategic post contributes to prevention and early detection of suspected Ebola cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Beni: Effectiveness of the Measure Limiting the Number of Passengers on Motorcycle Taxis - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Beni, Nord-Kivu, DRC: Authorities report a measure limiting passengers on motorcycle taxis to curb Ebola transmission. Officials warn transport can fuel transmission if barrier measures are ignored. Beni-based motorcycle-taxi drivers and the Amotav association back the action as crucial to cut the transmission chain, noting risk to riders themselves. Other vehicle types have tighter caps: four passengers on taxi cars, six on jeeps, and cargo vehicles may carry only the driver and an assistant. The measures aim to boost adherence to public health practices and ensure rapid medical referral for suspected Ebola cases.

article.articleHeadline: Infectious Information 10/21/2026
article.articleSummary: Rabies exposure incidents are rising; seek post-exposure vaccination immediately if exposure is possible. Ebola tops 9,000 cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Kenya reporting eight confirmed linked cases after a citizen carried infection home. Avian influenza continues to infect birds and dairy cattle, with uncertain broader impact. West Nile virus is active in the United States, and cholera persists in Congo and Yemen. Salmonella outbreaks are noted in raw oysters. A single-dose HPV vaccine may suffice to expand protection in low-income countries, while a vaccine against invasive E. coli has failed in trials. Antibiotics in children and teens are linked to higher irritable bowel syndrome risk in young adulthood; sugar intake may worsen antibiotic disruption of the microbiome, including cancer patients.

article.articleHeadline: On the Frontlines of the Ebola Response, Dr Alain Mangolopa Kakule Fights to Save Lives
article.articleSummary: Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is led by WHO epidemiologist Dr Alain Mangolopa Kakule, coordinating responses to Ebola, mpox and cholera in North Kivu, Equateur and Ituri. In Lita, on July 5, deaths were recorded at the general hospital and in the community; doctors and nurses were infected, and a hygienist died caring for patients. With WHO support, three teams—disease surveillance, case management and safe and dignified burials—were established and trained, hundreds of health providers and hygienists trained, surveillance and IPC reinforced, and a treatment structure urgently set up. Dr Alain emphasizes that effective response combines surveillance, IPC, case management, risk communication and community engagement to strengthen local capacity. Work unfolds amid insecurity and limited access, but lives are saved; as one survivor’s joy shows, a life saved justifies continuing efforts.

Recommendations include washing hands with soap or using hand sanitizer before and after workouts, carrying disinfectant wipes to clean equipment, and avoiding touching the face with hands after gym use.

article.articleHeadline: Henan Case Report Identifies Chest-Wall Alveolar Echinococcosis Mimicking
article.articleSummary: 66-year-old woman from southern Henan Province, China, presented with a progressively enlarging, painful chest-wall mass. Imaging showed sternum and rib involvement; histopathology found 90 IgG4-positive plasma cells per high-power field with elevated IgG4, mimicking IgG4-related disease. Prednisone failed as the lesion enlarged and invaded the sternum, ribs, and anterior mediastinum. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of purulent aspirate identified Echinococcus multilocularis at 99.99% relative abundance, confirming chest-wall alveolar echinococcosis—the first reported case in Henan. The infection's source remained unidentified, and no clear link to western China endemics was established. Radical resection was not feasible; the patient began albendazole 400 mg daily. At two years, the lesion decreased from >60 mm to 17 mm with near-complete symptom resolution. This case underscores diagnostic overlap with IgG4-related disease and supports sequencing-based confirmation and long-term albendazole therapy for alveolar echinococcosis.

article.articleHeadline: Antibiotic-resistant Salmonella: 2,536 genomes reveal a risk throughout the entire supply chain.
article.articleSummary: 2,536 Salmonella enterica genomes from humans, pork and chicken products, farming environments, and related sources across 15 Chinese provinces (samples 2006–2022) reveal widespread antibiotic-resistance traits, analyzed in the Nature Communications study published Oct 20, 2026. Researchers found 421 resistance-associated features, about 88% on mobile genetic elements such as plasmids, facilitating gene transfer between bacteria. Forty traits were detected across all sources, signaling cross-sector risk beyond any single food or setting. Notably, isolates from asymptomatic food workers harbored diverse resistance genes, including those linked to carbapenems and colistin. Transmission pathways are not established; shared genes across sources indicate vigilance is needed for surveillance of asymptomatic individuals. Projections to 2050, integrating antibiotic use and socio-economic factors, suggest 84 of 101 high-risk traits rise, with beta-lactam genes (e.g., blaCTX-M-64, blaTEM-1) potentially reaching ~20% prevalence; plasmid-borne fluoroquinolone resistance may also increase. WHO-guided practices—hand hygiene, separate raw/cooked foods, thorough cooking, proper storage—and prudent antibiotic use remain essential.

article.articleHeadline: A kind-hearted influencer contracted a rare fungus and died suddenly at 27! They once braved ruins to rescue stray dogs; millions watched and cried.
article.articleSummary: 27-year-old Chinese influencer Qin Siyu from Baiyin, Gansu, known for rescuing stray animals, died after contracting a rare fungus, Emergomyces orientalis, which triggered secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. In October 2025 she helped rescue a wounded stray dog named 'Little Lucky' in a derelict building; the incident went viral. She developed a severe infection and was in the ICU for 22 days before death. Emergomyces orientalis is an environmental fungus found in soil and dust; human infection occurs via inhaled spores or contact with contaminated skin wounds and is not known to spread person-to-person. Immunocompromised individuals, including long-term steroid or immunosuppressant users, cancer therapy recipients, or people with HIV, are at higher risk; HLH complicates treatment and increases mortality. Public health guidance advises protective measures when handling stray animals and to seek prompt care if fever, chest tightness, or fatigue after exposure to soil, old buildings, or stray animals, and to inform clinicians of exposure history.

article.articleHeadline: Dr. Krasnov: COVID has joined the ranks of seasonal viral respiratory infections.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 has joined the ranks of seasonal respiratory infections in Russia, says Viktor Krasnov, head of the infectious diseases department at Privolzhsky Research Medical University. The coronavirus is no longer dangerous to healthy people, and distinguishing it from ordinary respiratory illnesses without a test is now essentially impossible. However, complications after infection remain more common among individuals with chronic diseases. Krasnov acknowledges that while lethal mutations are possible, significant viral changes would take years. This autumn, Russia may see new gene variants of Hong Kong-type and swine-origin influenza strains, for which population immunity could be insufficient, according to Anna Popova, head of Rospotrebnadzor. The topic was discussed by Evening Moscow with experts about the dangers, symptoms, and protection related to these viruses.

article.articleHeadline: Retrospective study links infections and outcome risks in Good syndrome
article.articleSummary: Good syndrome (thymoma with hypogammaglobulinemia and opportunistic infections) evaluated at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Beijing, China, from January 2015 to December 2024. Respiratory infections dominated, comprising 88.9% of infectious complications. The leading organisms across categories were Pseudomonas aeruginosa (bacteria, 22.2%), Candida species (fungi, 44.4%), and cytomegalovirus (CMV, virus, 55.6%). Autoimmune diseases were present in 44.4%, and another malignancy in 7.4%; radiotherapy or chemotherapy for thymoma occurred in 25.9%. The cohort’s mean age at onset was 57.8 years (SD 9.3), with 37% male; all patients experienced infection during follow-up. Cox regression linked older age (HR 1.270 per year, 95% CI 1.042–1.548, p=0.018) and each additional day of pre-infection corticosteroid use (HR 1.049, 95% CI 1.004–1.095, p=0.033) to worse outcomes. CMV associated with cellular immune deficiency; elevated CRP with phagocytic deficiency; ICU admission tied to pre-infection steroids and lymphopenia. Five immunodeficiency-based clusters observed; limitations include retrospective, single-hospital design.

article.articleHeadline: Chinese Pig Farmers Scramble to Sell Hogs at Deep Discounts Amid Suspected Swine Fever Outbreaks

Reported infection rates are high in Jiangxi (80–90% in hardest-hit areas), with spread to Henan and Hubei; some farms claim positive lab results from Henan Agricultural University, though verification is limited by censorship. Sick pigs may fetch 1–2 yuan per pound; healthy pigs rarely exceed 6 yuan. Farmers face disposal costs if animals die. National live hog price averaged 10.89 yuan/kg ($1.63/kg) in Oct 12–18, down from 11.07 yuan/kg the prior week.

article.articleHeadline: She underwent Chinese acupuncture and developed a rare neck infection: "Within hours she became paralyzed"
article.articleSummary: A 50-year-old healthy woman in Israel developed a rare cervical spinal infection suspected to be linked to a Chinese acupuncture session a week earlier. She initially presented with mild arm weakness at Rambam Health Care Campus; a CT was unrevealing, but within 36 hours she progressed to quadriparesis. Urgent MRI revealed large cervical neck abscesses pressing on the spinal cord; she underwent two consecutive emergency surgeries to decompress and drain the infections. No clear source was identified, but clinicians implicated the acupuncture as the probable cause. The International Journal of Spine Surgery published the case, noting that only about 20 similar instances exist in the literature, with most cases presenting within two weeks and often requiring surgical intervention. Postoperatively, she gradually improved to the ability to walk but retained significant neurological deficits, including urinary continence loss. The report underlines rapid diagnosis, timely imaging, and surgical decompression, along with strict asepsis during invasive procedures.

article.articleHeadline: The oldest plague outbreak in human history dates back 5,500 years; the key is the Siberian marmot.
article.articleSummary: Approximately 5,500 years ago near Lake Baikal in southeastern Siberia, the oldest known plague outbreak is linked to Yersinia pestis detected in the burials of hunter-gatherers. Researchers associate the ancient transmission with the Siberian marmot (Marmota sibirica); marmot teeth found in graves support close human–animal contact, and the species is described as the only plague vector with archaeological evidence. In the 1870s, a Siberian expedition reported marmot-associated plague and human infections, and Soviet-era plague control has been studied for decades. A 1910–1911 outbreak in Manchuria reportedly killed about 60,000 people, with local hunters attributing the disease to marmots. In Mongolia, marmots remain culturally valued, but illegal hunting persists; in 2019 a western Mongolian couple died after eating raw marmot innards, and in 2020 a 15-year-old hunter also died. Nature published the June 17, 2026 report; current date: 2026-10-21.

article.articleHeadline: C19orf18 modulates host susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection via remodeling of the gut microbiota and tryptophan metabolism - npj Biofilms and Microbiomes
article.articleSummary: Salmonella Typhimurium infection susceptibility is modulated by the host gene C19orf18, according to a study in npj Biofilms and Microbiomes. The work links host genetics to infection risk through remodeling of the gut microbiota and alterations in tryptophan metabolism. Researchers affiliated with Jilin Agricultural University (Changchun, China) and partner institutions report that C19orf18 influences microbial community structure and metabolite pathways connected to Salmonella outcomes. The article notes no specific funding and is published under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License. Published on 2026-10-21, the study provides mechanistic context for how host genetic factors intersect with microbiota–metabolite dynamics to shape susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium.

article.articleHeadline: FDA Approval Brings New Hope for Millions Living With Hepatitis B
article.articleSummary: FDA approves Hibsago (bepirovirsen), the first antisense oligonucleotide for chronic hepatitis B, offering long-term control without continuous antiviral therapy. In the B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled across 29 countries), about 20% of treated patients achieved undetectable HBV DNA and remained off antivirals for at least 6 months. Hibsago reduces viral RNA and proteins, lowering hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and potentially enabling a durable immune response. Chronic hepatitis B affects more than 240 million people worldwide and causes around 1.1 million deaths annually, with current treatments achieving sustained viral clearance in roughly 1–4%. The drug has regulatory approval in Japan; applications are under review in China and Europe. These findings reflect progress toward a functional cure as of 2026-10-21.

article.articleHeadline: Class closures associated with fewer norovirus cases in Xi'an schools
article.articleSummary: Norovirus outbreaks in Xi’an educational settings (schools and kindergartens) reported to the Xi’an Center for Disease Control and Prevention from Oct 2020–Feb 2023: 61 outbreaks analyzed, with 44 meeting complete-data criteria (72.13%). Pre-intervention class suspensions were associated with fewer new cases, fewer newly affected classes, and a shorter interval from CDC intervention to outbreak end, but no significant difference in terminal attack rate or overall outbreak duration. Paired Wilcoxon tests: new cases fewer (Z=-3.313, P=0.001); newly affected classes fewer (Z=-1.992, P=0.046); interval to end shorter (Z=-2.392, P=0.017); terminal attack rate (Z=-1.161, P=0.245) and duration (Z=-1.189, P=0.234) not significant. Multivariable regression linked lower cumulative cases to government-reported outbreaks, adequate ventilation, public ownership, pre-intervention class suspension, and no more than 15 cases at response; public institutions, especially kindergartens, showed lower totals. Shorter durations tied to intervention within 48 hours and ownership. Optimal timing: closures within 48 hours and no more than 15 initial cases. Limitations: observational, not randomized; findings specific to Xi’an educational settings.

article.articleHeadline: Travel Nearly Doubles Odds of Tuberculosis Test Conversion in Asian American Patients
article.articleSummary: Among 5,668 patients with no prior TB infection at a San Francisco Bay Area federally qualified health center, TB test conversion occurred in 3.0% (2.1 per 100 person-years); 3.2% with IGRA and 2.9% with TST. Documented international travel between tests associated with nearly twofold increased odds of conversion (adjusted OR 1.95; 95% CI 1.07–3.57). Among converters, 20% had travel vs 13% of non-converters, mostly to East or Southeast Asia. In the chart-reviewed subset of 119 converters, 100 diagnosed with latent TB infection; 57% initiated treatment and 65% completed it. TB disease developed within 5 years of estimated infection in two routinely tested patients and in eight converters overall; among four with available Interferon-Gamma Release Assay values, all had high-positive results. Supports considering travel in risk-based TB testing in low-prevalence settings.

article.articleHeadline: Pulmonary tuberculosis spares no one, not even the young: A warning from hundreds of new cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 October 2026, Hospital 19-8 in Vietnam reports hundreds of new pulmonary tuberculosis cases, with a large share among young people. Many patients have had a cough for 3–4 months before seeking care, by which time lung damage is already advanced, increasing transmission risk. Warning signs include a cough lasting more than two weeks (dry, productive, sometimes blood-tinged), evening fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Diagnosis relies on sputum smear microscopy and GeneXpert to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance, complemented by chest X-ray; the hospital also offers CT chest, microbiology and molecular testing, sputum culture, and bronchoscopy. Treatment adheres to national TB protocols; stopping meds prematurely can lead to drug-resistant TB. Preventive measures include masking around suspected cases, proper ventilation, and prompt medical evaluation for prolonged cough, which improves outcomes and reduces community spread.

article.articleHeadline: Be vigilant against infectious diseases at the end of the year.
article.articleSummary: An Giang province reports rising dengue fever and hand-foot-mouth disease as the rainy season promotes mosquito breeding. From January to October, dengue cases total 7,384 with 1 death and over 2,000 outbreak clusters; hand-foot-mouth exceeds 6,000 cases with 1 death. October and November are peak months, prompting intensified surveillance, early outbreak detection, rapid isolation capacity, and public messaging. Health authorities have reviewed facilities, ensured bed capacity, and are prepared to add beds if patient numbers surge; stock emergency medicines, IV fluids, blood products, consumables, mosquito-control chemicals, and Chloramine B for disinfection. For households, emphasis on sleeping under nets, covering water containers, clearing vegetation, and seeking prompt care. Parents should follow vaccination schedules and maintain personal hygiene. The 26 regional centers and 106 commune health stations, with local authorities and schools, are boosting community sanitation, larval source reduction, and outreach via radio and digital platforms, encouraging weekly 10-minute cleanups.

article.articleHeadline: Climate change raises temperatures, and diseases could become more complex.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam's 2025 climate-change scenario (SSP-based) projects rising maximum temperatures nationwide and rising minimum temperatures, especially in the North. By 2100, South China Sea sea level is projected to rise 46.1–63.7 cm (low-high), with Vietnam’s coast averaging about 61.9 cm and upper bounds near 82.0 cm; the Mekong Delta faces the highest flood risk. Heat days (over 35°C) are expected to rise by 10–30 days at 1.5°C warming and 30–50 days at 3–4°C. Rice yields decline in the Red River Delta and Mekong Delta; Mekong Delta is more sensitive, with losses exceeding 10% in some crops at 4°C warming. Dengue fever risk and WBGT > 32°C heat-health conditions are projected to rise in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Adaptation emphasizes green spaces, reflective materials, passive cooling, and climate-resilient urban planning to reduce heat and energy demand.

article.articleHeadline: Saving the life of an 8-year-old girl in Dong Nai Province with severe dengue complications.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever severely affected an 8-year-old girl in Dong Nai Province, Vietnam. Admitted in early August to Dong Nai Children’s Hospital with high fever, abdominal pain and vomiting, she rapidly progressed to multi-organ failure: respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation, abdominal compartment syndrome with anuria from kidney failure, and severe coagulopathy. Liver enzymes soared to over 24,500 U/L (about 600× normal). ICU implemented ventilatory support, abdominal drainage, transfusions, two plasma exchanges, and 17 renal replacement therapy sessions. She developed complications including antibiotic-resistant bacterial pneumonia, fungal pneumonia, bladder hemorrhage, and severe liver injury. After over a month of intervention, liver and kidney function improved, and by 13 October she was alert, able to sit, eat, and converse. She was discharged after more than two months. The case underscores vigilance in dengue management and warns against ibuprofen/aspirin use and unsupervised IV fluids. Da Nang faces rising dengue outbreaks, prompting vector control efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Sevuparin 3 mg/kg dose selected in children with severe malaria
article.articleSummary: Phase I open-label dose-escalation trial in Kenya (Kilifi County Hospital) and Zambia (Saint Paul’s Hospital, Nchelenge) evaluated sevuparin as an adjunct to intravenous artesunate for severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children aged 3 months–12 years. Twenty analyzed of 23 enrolled between Sept 2022 and Mar 2025; dosing cohorts tested 1.5, 3, 4, 4.5, 5, and 6 mg/kg. Primary toxicity endpoint was activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) >95 seconds (2.5× ULN). Dose-limiting coagulation abnormalities occurred at 4–6 mg/kg; no DLTs at 3 mg/kg, leading to 3 mg/kg as the maximum tolerated dose for further study. Adherence was 100%; six of 20 analyzed (30%) had APTT >95 seconds, but events were transient and non-bleeding, with no events at 24 hours. The trial confirms safety, not efficacy, and notes severe malaria’s high pediatric mortality in sub-Saharan Africa and PfEMP1-mediated microvascular sequestration as the biological target.

article.articleHeadline: Tropical Disease: Dengue: Caution Advised at These Long-Distance Travel Destinations.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a travel health risk for Brazil, Florida, Cuba, and the Philippines, with current high case numbers cited by CRM—Centrum für Reisemedizin. Transmission by day-biting Aedes mosquitoes; many infections are asymptomatic. When symptoms occur, typical signs include high fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, retro-orbital pain, and a widespread rash, usually appearing 4–7 days post-infection, and up to two weeks in some cases. A minority develop severe disease with abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and mucosal bleeding, which can be fatal. Travelers are urged to strengthen mosquito protection and consult the ECDC for real-time dengue outbreaks before travel. Pre-travel medical counseling can assess risk and evaluate dengue vaccination eligibility. After returning, continue protection for 14 days to prevent local transmission by mosquitoes. If fever occurs during or after travel, seek medical evaluation and disclose travel history.

article.articleHeadline: Anticipating the Spread of Anthrax, Bantul DKPP Officers Routinely Monitor Livestock Markets.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 October 2026, Bantul Regency in DI Yogyakarta conducts routine surveillance of livestock movements at animal markets and border areas to prevent anthrax spread. Bantul’s Dinas Ketahanan Pangan dan Pertanian (DKPP) reports market staff and Puskeswan personnel monitor animal health and inspect incoming livestock for clinical signs. Farmers are urged to report any suspected cases to nearby Puskeswan for early containment, with ongoing socialization and education on recognizing illness in livestock. Although anthrax has occurred in a neighboring district, there are no reported cases in Bantul livestock, and the program aims to keep traded animals healthy and reassure farmers and traders about safety at markets.

article.articleHeadline: 7 Signs of Mosquito Breeding Grounds Around the House That Are Rarely Inspected, Trigger Dengue Fever Outbreaks During the Rainy Season
article.articleSummary: As of 21 October 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia, health authorities warn that dengue fever (DBD) outbreaks spike during the rainy season when mosquitoes breed in domestic water containers. The article outlines seven household inspection targets to identify and eliminate breeding sites. Indoors, mosquitoes breed around hidden areas such as under tables, behind wardrobes, under beds, and other seldom-cleaned corners; adults may enter from outdoors to rest in sheltered spots. After rainfall, check for standing water in containers: bathtubs, buckets, pet waterers, vases, and other vessels; empty, scrub, and store items properly. Aedes mosquito eggs can cling to the inside walls of containers that once held water and hatch when refilled. Gutters, downspouts, and blocked drains can create rainwater stagnation; clean them after rain. The Ministry of Health promotes 3M Plus—drain, cover, recycle, and other prevention measures—to reduce breeding grounds.

article.articleHeadline: Papua Highlands to Boost Veterinary Health Services to Prevent Livestock Diseases
article.articleSummary: Papua Highlands Province, Indonesia, is expanding veterinary health services in Mamberamo Tengah Regency to prevent livestock diseases, especially African Swine Fever (ASF). During a Kobakma District visit, field staff collected blood samples from pigs and provided on-site treatments as part of routine surveillance. Samples were sent to Balai Besar Veteriner Jayapura for full testing to detect ASF. The surveillance program spans eight districts; Mamberamo Tengah is the fourth visited, after Yalimo, Lanny Jaya, and Tolikara. The remaining districts yet to be covered are Jayawijaya, Nduga, Yahukimo, and Pegunungan Bintang, with three of these accessed by air. The initiative aims to monitor pig health and prevent ASF spread amid reports of the virus circulating in Indonesia, particularly Papua, though the article does not report any confirmed cases yet.

article.articleHeadline: Cases of stray dog bites on the rise in Halong, Balangan, with victims numbering up to eight people from several villages.
article.articleSummary: Eight people from several villages in Halong subdistrict, Balangan Regency, Indonesia, have been bitten by stray dogs, with five October cases recorded at Puskesmas Halong (Bangkal, Kapul, Mantuyan, Padang Raya, Mamantang; one treated in hospital) and three cases at Puskesmas Uren (Binuang, Mauya, Mamigang). By 21 October 2026, October surge follows September cases in Binuang, Mauya, and Marajai, some of which were severe and referred to hospital. Authorities apply a rapid, precautionary approach: all bite victims receive Rabies Vaccine (VAR), and those with heavy or high-risk wounds also receive Rabies Immunoglobulin (SAR). VAR induces gradual antibody development; SAR provides immediate neutralizing antibodies. In response to rising cases, Puskesmas coordinates with the Animal Health Office to intensify canine rabies vaccination and conducts outreach with Forkopimcam Halong, Police, TNI, KUA, the District Education Office, and village heads to strengthen prevention and awareness.

article.articleHeadline: South Central Timor Regency Government–UNICEF Workshop to Strengthen Pediatric TB Control and Stop Local Malaria Transmission
article.articleSummary: South Central Timor Regency (TTS), East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, with UNICEF, held a workshop in Soe on Oct 20, 2026 to optimize detection and diagnosis of pediatric tuberculosis (TB) at primary health facilities and to pursue zero Indigenous malaria by 2026. Participants included puskesmas, hospitals, PAUD, Bappeda, Dinas Pendidikan, and UNICEF. From January–September 2026, TTS reported 45 pediatric TB cases and screened 55,746 people for TB. Challenges include case finding, contact tracing, TB preventive therapy, and access to diagnosis and treatment. The district pledges Zero TB in Children and Zero Local Malaria, with strengthened screening via the Integrated Management of Sick Under-Fives (MTBS), KIA, and immunization, plus contact investigations. Malaria remains a concern: as of Oct 15, 2026, 77 Indigenous cases, API 0.16 per 1,000; last indigenous case Sept 2026; hotspots Boking and Nunkolo. ABER: Boking 36.65%, Nunkolo 23.44%.

article.articleHeadline: Swine fever: Cologne experts want to save animals.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) threatens Asia’s wild boar species, with 12 species potentially facing extinction and six already experiencing mass die-offs. Cologne Zoo’s Sulawesi warty pig exemplifies the crisis as two Cologne experts collaborate with 31 scientists to draft an IUCN action plan. Since ASF was introduced to Asia by humans in 2018, the virus kills about 95% of infected pigs, jeopardizing wild populations. Transmission spreads via human activity, including contaminated food—one truck driver discarded an infected salami bread in the Netherlands—and through surfaces like tires and footwear, hindering protection in the field. If wild species vanish, ecological roles and predator-prey dynamics suffer, exemplified by hunger-driven tiger raids on Sumatra villages. The IUCN roadmap stresses biosafety, pork testing, emergency and early-warning systems. Zoos could host back-up populations for potential future rewilding, but there is no vaccine yet.

article.articleHeadline: Kediri Health Office strengthens surveillance to prevent disease outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: Kediri City Health Office in East Java, Indonesia, strengthens surveillance and mobilizes health cadres and surveillance officers to detect early vaccine-preventable diseases (PD3I) and prevent extraordinary events (KLB). Acting head Dr. Rini Hidayat says cadres, who interact with communities, will identify suspicious symptoms early and relay information on immunization benefits, schedules, and completion. Epidemiological surveillance aims to detect and monitor possible cases promptly to prevent wider transmission and lower KLB risk. Diseases preventable by vaccination include diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B, human papillomavirus infection, measles, and rubella. The city notes declining immunization coverage and urges strengthening public understanding while addressing misinformation about adverse events after immunization (KIPI). It calls for timely consultation with health workers and emphasizes complete immunization, active surveillance, and community participation to enhance PD3I protection.

article.articleHeadline: The Mojokerto City Government and the Ministry of Social Affairs provide ATENSI assistance to TB survivors.
article.articleSummary: Mojokerto City government and the Indonesian Ministry of Social Affairs distributed Bantuan Asistensi Rehabilitasi Sosial (ATENSI) to 46 tuberculosis (TB) survivors in Mojokerto. The aid, provided via Sentra Margo Laras in Pati and handed over at Pendapa Sabha Mandala Tama, Balai Kota Mojokerto, comprises a package worth Rp1,809,580 per recipient, including groceries, nutritional support, and household items (plastic cabinet, fan, mat). As of 21 October 2026, 46 TB survivors received the assistance. The program acknowledges those who completed six months of TB treatment and were declared cured, aiming to motivate others to adhere to medications to reduce transmission and protect vulnerable groups such as children. article.articleHeadline: Madiun Regency engages cross-OPD agencies and institutions to expand TB detection.
article.articleSummary: As of 21 October 2026, Madiun Regency, East Java, is expanding tuberculosis (TB) detection by mobilizing cross-OPD agencies and institutions. Sekda Sigit Budiarto said TB screening is no longer confined to the local health office (Dinkes) but also engages the Education Department, the Department for Village Community Empowerment (DPMD), and the Ministry of Religious Affairs (Kemenag) to reach more targets, including pondok pesantren, students, and prospective brides in villages. The effort involves all OPD units, the district military command (Kodim), the district attorney (Kejari), Kecamatan offices, Puskesmas, villages, universities, and professional associations. Anies Djaka Karyawan of the Health Office noted that among roughly 10,000 people screened with a mobile X-ray unit, 1,200 new TB cases were found. TB prevention is integrated with housing improvement (RTLH) and sanitation programs. Initiatives also include education campaigns, village-level screening with Puskesmas and Integrated Primary Services (ILP), and free health checks. The goal is TB elimination by 2030.

article.articleHeadline: Grandma Never Got Vaccinated in Her Life! Went to Thailand, Contracted Influenza, and Stayed in the ICU for Over a Month; Medical Bills Exceed 600,000.
article.articleSummary: An nearly 80-year-old woman in Taiwan who had never been vaccinated against influenza contracted influenza during a July–August 2026 trip to Thailand and spent over a month in an ICU abroad; back in Taiwan, with diabetes and poor lung health, she incurred over NT$600,000 in medical costs before returning and getting vaccinated. Taiwan’s influenza activity remains in the epidemic period: for the week Oct 11–17, 2026, 159 influenza cases with severe complications and 44 deaths were reported (151 H1N1, 7 influenza A, 1 B; 42 H1N1 and 2 A deaths). Officials warn the outbreak may ease by early November with improved vaccine coverage; public-funded antivirals have been extended to Nov 15. Separately, COVID vaccination also reduces severe outcomes; a meta-analysis shows 40% reduction in composite cardiovascular/cerebrovascular events, 25% less ischemic stroke, and 30% less acute coronary syndromes. Health coin incentives boosted elderly vaccination; free vaccines began Oct 1, with ~3.4 million flu doses and ~1.07 million COVID doses by Oct 19, and Novavax added for those 12+.

article.articleHeadline: First a mild fever, then the condition worsens! This tiny bug preys on children.
article.articleSummary: Scrub typhus risk from tiny mite bites in rural Bihar, India. Begusarai Sadar Hospital reports mite larvae bites can trigger scrub typhus; risk rises in summer and monsoon among shrubs and tall grasses around homes. In the past two months, about 50 children were treated for mite-related typhus-like illness. Early bite-site lesions may be a small wound or black crust; initial symptoms resemble fever, but children can develop high fever, fatigue, red eyes, headaches, body pains, and sometimes rash. Diagnosis requires laboratory confirmation; delays can lead to serious organ involvement, including brain. Prevention: avoid playing in dense grass, wear full-coverage clothing, and check the body after outdoor play. Do not self-medicate; seek medical care promptly for persistent fever or unusual skin lesions. Doctors should consider scrub typhus in persistent pediatric fever in rural settings.

article.articleHeadline: Gadchiroli's Malaria Burden Tests India's 2030 Goal
article.articleSummary: Malaria persists in Laheri PHC, Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra, threatening India's 2030 elimination target. Laheri, serving 43 villages with about 10,688 people, posted an Annual Parasite Index (API) of 199.59 in 2025, far above the transmission threshold of 2, while Gadchiroli accounts for roughly half of Maharashtra's malaria despite ~1% of the state population. Repeated infections are common: in this year, the Timma family and others report multiple positive tests; Laheri’s records show 2024: 18 patients with two infections, 3 with three, 2 with four, 2 with five; 2025: 16 twice, 5 thrice, 1 four; 2026 so far: 14 twice, 2 thrice. Plasmodium falciparum remains the most common parasite, followed by P. vivax, with occasional P. malariae and P. ovale. Challenges include difficult terrain, forest–field mobility, and limited health access; emphasis on knowledge, nets, indoor spraying, and sustained ASHA-led outreach.

article.articleHeadline: Coimbatore Corporation to hold special medical camps to combat monsoon-related infections
article.articleSummary: Coimbatore Corporation organized a five-day special medical camp in areas with stagnant rainwater to prevent monsoon-related infections. Through 33 urban primary health centres, public health teams are visiting affected neighborhoods to screen residents for fever and other illnesses; individuals needing further tests are referred to government hospitals for blood tests and treatment. On Oct 20, the first day, 1,813 people benefited, with nine presenting fever warranting blood tests. Preventive measures include urging boiled and cooled water to curb waterborne diseases such as diarrhoea, typhoid, jaundice, and leptospirosis; water supply is tested for chlorine levels; cleaning drives and disinfectant spraying are conducted. ORS and kabasura kudineer are distributed to residents. This initiative underscores local public health response to post-rain health risks in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu.

article.articleHeadline: Systematic review finds bacterial contamination on 79.3% of African
article.articleSummary: Systematic review across Africa finds 79.3% of circulating currency notes contaminated with bacteria (95% CI 60.9–90.4%), based on 12 studies and 2,003 notes; 1,455 notes were contaminated (crude 72.6%). Nigeria contributed 60.9% of eligible evidence; Ghana and South Sudan showed complete contamination in small studies. Bacteria identified in pooled data: Staphylococcus aureus (31.2% of isolates) and Escherichia coli (24.0%), with Klebsiella, Salmonella, Pseudomonas, Proteus and Shigella frequently reported. Antimicrobial resistance reported in several studies, including MRSA and multidrug-resistant isolates; common resistances to ampicillin, penicillin, tetracycline, cotrimoxazole, and erythromycin. Higher contamination on lower-denomination, worn notes; polymer notes less contaminated. Samples drawn from markets, food-vending sites, butcher shops, restaurants, hospitals, banks, universities and transport settings. Limitations: high heterogeneity, English-language only, potential publication bias; currency contamination does not prove infection. Recommendations: hand hygiene, avoiding handling food and money together, improved currency management, and One Health surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Ghana Sets a 2030 Deadline For Raw Ore, a Fragile Peace Searches For Footing, and Ebola Reaches Abuja: One Week, One Lesson.
article.articleSummary: Ebola reaches Abuja; Ghana will pursue a ban on raw ore exports by 2030, covering bauxite, manganese, iron and lithium, backed by legislation. The Minerals and Mining Bill would let the minister prohibit raw concentrate exports by regulation (Section 110), but the 2030 deadline is not law and enforcement would fall to a successor; government aims for at least one LBMA-accredited refinery by 2030. Industry urges immediate contract reform to enable local processing. Security updates: the Security and Intelligence Agencies Act 2026 (Act 1168) was assented; regional ministers briefed; National Security Strategy under review; Ghana-EU partnership with defence support via the European Peace Facility, linked to Burkina Faso attacks on Ghanaian traders. Obuasi SHTS headmaster Zakaria Abdulai suspended amid investigations; 16 students have come forward; due process and student protection stressed.
